doctrine.label: B2B Invoicing, Photography Licensing + IP, Contract Essentials, Tax Mechanics

1_payment_terms_taxonomy.label: B2B Payment Terms Taxonomy + Decision Logic
core_rules: Cash: zero credit risk, use with new/unknown clients or high-risk transactions.
CBS (Cash Before Shipment): all funds received before work begins; use for custom/non-resalable deliverables.
CIA (Cash In Advance): full payment before any work; appropriate for high-risk clients or bespoke digital work.
CND (Cash Next Delivery): prior invoice paid before next delivery; enforces discipline with repeat clients without cutting them off.
COD (Cash On Delivery): payment at handoff; eliminates credit but requires logistics coordination.
CWO (Cash With Order): payment accompanies purchase order; reduces AR exposure on new client relationships.
Contra Payment: offset invoices between two parties who buy from each other; eliminates cash movement, reduces AR/AP simultaneously. Underutilized.
EOM (End of Month): all invoices in the billing month due at month-end; simplifies AR cycle for recurring client work.
Net X (Net 15/30/45/60): standard credit terms; longer nets favor larger clients/bigger contracts. Calibrate by relationship stage and cash flow need.
2/10 Net 30: 2% discount if paid within 10 days, full balance due day 30; incentivizes fast payment without penalty.
Interest Invoice: charge interest on overdue balances; must be disclosed in contract in advance. Use with serial late-payers after first warning.
Terms of Sale: umbrella term covering all conditions; document explicitly every time, never rely on verbal agreement.
1MD / Forward Dating: invoice dated for future delivery; useful for managing client cash flow on larger projects. Underutilized by small operators.
decision_heuristics: New client, unknown creditworthiness: CIA or CBS.
Trusted repeat client, project-based: Net 30 or EOM.
Both parties transacting with each other: Contra.
Client wants extended terms, you need cash: 2/10 Net 30 to pull payment forward.
Recurring serial late-payer: Interest Invoice clause, pre-disclosed in contract.
Large custom deliverable, non-resalable: CWO or CBS minimum.

2_photography_licensing_and_ip.label: Photography Copyright, Licensing + Three-Component Pricing
core_rules: Photographer owns the copyright at the moment of capture by default under US copyright law. Clients purchase a license, not ownership.
Copyright transfer (full assignment) is a separate transaction from a license and commands a significant premium. Never bundle it into a standard package price.
All usage requires written permission. Verbal agreements are unenforceable on IP.
Photographer retains copyright even after full payment unless a written assignment is signed.
Usage rights language in contracts must be explicit: specify medium, term, region, exclusivity. Ambiguity defaults in favor of the photographer.

licensing_fee_variables.exclusivity_premium: Exclusivity adds a multiplier on top of use/term/region base rate. Non-exclusive is default unless exclusivity is explicitly sold.

three_component_pricing_structure.component_1: Production expenses (hard costs: studio, lighting, travel, wardrobe, MUA, etc.)
three_component_pricing_structure.component_3: Rights/usage fee (licensing value driven by use/term/region/exclusivity variables above)
three_component_pricing_structure.invoicing_rule: Bundle all three into a single line-item invoice for small brands. Itemize each separately for large/corporate brands (they expect line-item breakdowns and separate licensing line items).

wedding_video: Full payment schedule: deposit + balance due date.
Cancellation and rescheduling terms with penalty tiers.
What is and is not included (number of cameras, hours of coverage, raw footage policy).
Music licensing responsibility (typically client's if they select copyrighted music).
Copyright ownership: photographer/videographer retains; portfolio use rights reserved.
Liability cap: maximum liability equals the contract fee.

3_tax_and_bookkeeping_mechanics.label: Tax Deduction Substantiation + Bookkeeping Discipline
core_rules: Substantiation rule: every deduction requires documentation of amount, date, business purpose, and who was present (for meals/entertainment).

Equipment depreciation: Section 179 allows full first-year expensing of qualifying equipment (cameras, lenses, computers, lighting) up to annual limit. Bonus depreciation may apply to remainder. Timing matters: buy before year-end to capture current-year deduction.
Business meals: 50% deductible. Requires receipt + note of business purpose + attendees. Personal meals are not deductible.

Vehicle: two methods. Standard mileage rate (track every business mile, log date/destination/purpose) OR actual expense method (track all vehicle costs + business-use percentage). Pick one method per vehicle and hold it.
Home office: must be used regularly and exclusively for business. Deduct actual square footage ratio OR simplified $5/sq ft up to 300 sq ft.
Bookkeeping minimum cadence: reconcile monthly, not annually. Annual reconciliation at tax time surfaces errors too late to correct.
Separate business and personal accounts. Commingling creates audit risk and makes bookkeeping 5-10x harder.
Federal contracting procedural note: invoicing and payment terms in government contracts follow specific FAR clauses; standard Net 30 baseline with Prompt Payment Act protections for contractors.

4_contract_best_practices_community.label: Photography Contract Essentials (Community-Validated)
core_rules: Have an attorney review any contract template before using it commercially. Community templates are starting points, not final instruments.
Non-negotiable contract essentials: deposit/retainer amount, cancellation policy, copyright/IP clause, delivery timeline, scope of work definition, limitation of liability.
CRM tools with built-in contract/invoice workflows reduce friction and enforce consistency (e.g., HoneyBook, Dubsado, Studio Ninja).
Force majeure and weather/illness clauses are non-optional for outdoor or event photography.
Second-shooter and subcontractor language: if you use them, contract must address who owns the images they capture.
Social media usage clause: address whether clients can tag/credit your work and whether you retain the right to post for portfolio purposes.
Late fees for image delivery should be avoided; instead, set conservative delivery timelines and build buffer in.

notes: Source is a mixed-format document: marketing blog content (payment terms), video transcripts (photography contracts + licensing), instructional/boilerplate text (tax/bookkeeping), and Reddit thread UI scaffolding with embedded community Q&A. Signal is medium: real usable mechanics exist across all four sections but none represent original proprietary frameworks. No SNIPED-exclusive methodology. Directly applicable to: SNIPED client invoicing architecture, licensing fee structure for Brand Systems and Track B, contract clause design, and year-end tax deduction capture. Three-component pricing structure (production + creative fee + rights) and Contra payment method are the highest-leverage underutilized concepts in the doc.
